Disclosed are an array substrate and a liquid crystal display panel. The array substrate includes a plurality of gate lines and a plurality of data lines. The plurality of gate lines and the plurality of data lines are interleaved to form a plurality of pixel areas, and a pixel electrode is formed in each of the pixel areas. The pixel electrode is connected to a corresponding gate line and a corresponding data line via a thin film transistor. The array substrate further includes a common electrode, which is connected to a first pixel electrode and a second electrode via a thin film transistor. A signal in the first pixel electrode and a signal in the second pixel electrode have opposite polarities. The array substrate realizes automatic adjustment of a common electrode voltage, and corresponding regulators or machines are no longer needed. It is favorable to improvement of productivity and competitiveness of the array substrate and the liquid crystal display panel.

outputs.L2: An array substrate and a liquid crystal display panel are provided. The substrate comprises multiple gate lines crossing multiple data lines, thereby defining numerous pixel regions. Each pixel region contains a pixel electrode coupled to its associated gate line and data line through a thin-film transistor. The substrate additionally comprises a common electrode connected through a thin-film transistor to a first pixel electrode and a second electrode. The signals of the first and second pixel electrodes have mutually opposite polarities. This configuration enables the common-electrode voltage to be adjusted automatically, eliminating the need for separate regulating devices or equipment. Consequently, the productivity and market competitiveness of both the array substrate and the liquid crystal display panel can be improved.
outputs.L3:
The array substrate includes a plurality of gate lines and data lines arranged in an interleaved pattern to define multiple pixel areas. Each pixel area includes a pixel electrode electrically connected to the corresponding gate line and data line through a thin-film transistor, which controls the application of a data signal to the pixel electrode.

The substrate further includes a common electrode coupled, through a thin-film transistor, to a first pixel electrode and a second pixel electrode. The signals applied to the first and second pixel electrodes have opposite polarities. By using these opposite-polarity signals, the structure automatically adjusts the voltage of the common electrode to an appropriate level.

As a result, the common-electrode voltage can be regulated without a separate voltage regulator or dedicated adjustment equipment. This simplifies the manufacturing process, reduces equipment and production costs, and improves both productivity and product competitiveness.
outputs.L4:
An array substrate for a liquid crystal display panel includes a plurality of gate lines and data lines arranged to intersect one another, thereby defining a matrix of pixel regions. A thin-film transistor is disposed in each pixel region and is electrically connected to a corresponding gate line and data line. Each thin-film transistor selectively supplies a data signal to an associated pixel electrode in response to a gate signal. The substrate further includes a common electrode that cooperates with the pixel electrodes to generate electric fields for controlling the orientation of liquid-crystal molecules.

The common electrode is electrically coupled to at least two pixel electrodes to which data signals having opposite polarities are applied. Because the opposite-polarity signals compensate for one another, the voltage of the common electrode is automatically adjusted to an appropriate level. This self-adjusting arrangement reduces common-voltage fluctuations and supports stable operation and uniform image quality without requiring a separate external voltage regulator, adjustment circuit, or dedicated calibration equipment. As a result, the structure simplifies panel fabrication and testing, reduces manufacturing cost and process time, and improves both productivity and product competitiveness.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an array substrate and liquid crystal display panel that automatically adjusts the common electrode voltage using pixel electrodes with opposite signal polarities.
counterfactuals.output: An array substrate and a liquid crystal display panel are disclosed. The array substrate includes a plurality of pixel units, a common electrode, and a common-voltage adjustment circuit. The plurality of pixel units includes a first pixel electrode receiving a first data signal and a second pixel electrode receiving a second data signal having a polarity opposite to that of the first data signal with respect to a common electrode voltage. The common-voltage adjustment circuit is electrically coupled to the first and second pixel electrodes and is configured to obtain a feedback signal based on voltages of the first and second pixel electrodes, determine an offset of the common electrode voltage according to the feedback signal, and adjust the common electrode voltage to reduce the offset. By using pixel electrodes having opposite signal polarities to generate the feedback signal, common-mode signal components may be suppressed and common electrode voltage deviation may be detected and compensated automatically, thereby reducing flicker, image sticking, and display nonuniformity and improving display quality.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise technical disclosure describing an LCD array substrate that eliminates the need for external common-voltage regulators and improves manufacturing productivity and competitiveness.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Disclosure: LCD Array Substrate with Integrated Common-Voltage Generation

An LCD array substrate includes a display area having gate lines, data lines, pixel electrodes, and switching elements, together with a common-electrode line configured to supply a common voltage to a common electrode. A common-voltage generation circuit is formed directly on a peripheral region of the array substrate using the same thin-film transistor and conductive-layer processes employed to form the pixel array and gate-driving circuitry.

The common-voltage generation circuit receives one or more existing panel supply voltages and generates a predetermined common voltage through an integrated voltage-dividing network. A thin-film-transistor buffer may isolate the voltage-dividing network from the common-electrode load and distribute the generated voltage through multiple low-resistance common-voltage buses. Optional programmable switches, fusible links, or trimming resistors permit adjustment of the common voltage to compensate for process variation and minimize flicker or image sticking.

By generating and conditioning the common voltage on the array substrate, the design eliminates a separate external common-voltage regulator and associated integrated circuits, wiring, terminals, and assembly operations. Integration reduces component count, panel cost, bezel or module area, and manufacturing complexity while improving production yield, throughput, reliability, and product competitiveness.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for a display panel in which interleaved gate and data lines define pixel areas, each pixel electrode is TFT-connected, and the common electrode voltage is adjusted automatically.
counterfactuals.output: A display panel includes a plurality of gate lines and data lines arranged in an interleaved, intersecting pattern to define a plurality of pixel areas. Each pixel area includes a pixel electrode and a thin-film transistor electrically connecting the pixel electrode to a corresponding data line in response to a gate signal supplied through a corresponding gate line. A common electrode is disposed to form a pixel capacitance with the pixel electrodes and receives a common electrode voltage. A voltage adjustment circuit automatically adjusts the common electrode voltage based on at least one detected panel operating condition, such as a data-signal level, a gate-signal transition, a frame polarity, a panel load, or a feedback voltage detected from the common electrode. A controller determines a compensation value and controls the voltage adjustment circuit to reduce common-voltage deviation caused by parasitic coupling or signal transitions. Accordingly, display artifacts including flicker, crosstalk, and image nonuniformity may be reduced.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in formal patent language, an array substrate whose common electrode is connected through a thin-film transistor to first and second electrodes carrying signals of opposite polarities.
counterfactuals.output: An array substrate comprises a base substrate, a common electrode disposed on the base substrate, a first signal electrode configured to receive a first electrical signal, a second signal electrode configured to receive a second electrical signal having a polarity opposite to that of the first electrical signal, and a thin-film transistor electrically coupled to the common electrode and the first and second signal electrodes. The thin-film transistor includes a gate electrode electrically connected to the first signal electrode, a first source/drain electrode electrically connected to the second signal electrode, and a second source/drain electrode electrically connected to the common electrode. In response to the first electrical signal applied to the gate electrode, the thin-film transistor selectively establishes a conductive path between the second signal electrode and the common electrode, thereby transmitting the second electrical signal to the common electrode. The oppositely polarized first and second electrical signals may be defined relative to a common reference potential and may be used to control or stabilize a potential of the common electrode.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
